title: Poly(2-ethyl-2-oxazoline)-based draw solutes for forward osmosis: performance evaluation and draw solute recovery
content: In this study, poly(2-ethyl-2-oxazoline) (PEOZ) homopolymers were introduced as novel draw solutes for forward osmosis (FO), representing the first reported exploration of PEOZ in FO systems. PEOZ homopolymers with molecular weights of 2000, 5000, and 10 000 g mol−1 were synthesized and characterized by 1H NMR, FTIR, DSC, TGA, and SEC analyses. Aqueous 50% (w/v) PEOZ (2 kDa, 5 kDa, 10 kDa) solutions were evaluated as draw solutes against ultra-pure water (UPW) feed and 2000 ppm NaCl feed solution to assess the effect of molecular weight on FO performance. With UPW feed, PEOZ 2 kDa achieved the highest water flux of 16 L m−2 h−1 with a reverse solute flux (RSF) of 0.37 g m−2 h−1, while with 2000 ppm NaCl feed, the flux and reverse solute flux were 14.5 L m−2 h−1 and 0.22 g m−2 h−1, respectively. To recover the diluted draw solutions, two different regeneration routes were independently evaluated: (1) ultrafiltration (UF), which achieved over 99% polymer retention for all PEOZ molecular weights, and (2) membrane distillation (MD), which reconcentrated the draw solutions from 10% to 50% (w/v) at 70 °C while maintaining very low reverse polymer flux (0.094–0.165 g m−2 h−1). These results demonstrate the potential of PEOZ homopolymers as draw solutes for FO-based desalination and water treatment applications, providing elevated water flux, minimal reverse solute flux, and effective recovery.
